newsitem.title: BELARUS: Lukashenko blasts Russia in sign links worsening.
newsitem.headline: Lukashenko blasts Russia in sign links worsening.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko on Friday slammed neighbouring Russia for checking up on his border guards' work in a sign of worsening relations linked to the detention of two Russian television crews in Belarus.

Interfax-West news agency quoted the leader of the country of 10 million, whose authoritarian style of rule has been criticised in the West, as defending the second arrest of a Russian TV crew on the border with Lithuania in three weeks.

"Three are imprisoned, one is freed, and now another four went in. What can you say? What are you doing, creeping up to the border? What are four people doing there all at once?" he was quoted as saying on a visit to the western town of Brest.
He was responding to the detention of four members of a camera crew from Russia's ORT channel in a near-replay of events on July 26, when another ORT crew was detained at the same border.
Interfax later reported that the second crew had been released from a police station but it was not clear if any charges would be pressed against them at a later stage.

Pavel Sheremet, correspondent with the first crew, attracted the wrath of Belarussian authorities by jumping across a border fence and was arrested with three colleagues. The driver was freed pending trial but two of the four face a possible five years in jail.
"Pavel Sheremet has already shown that this border only exists on paper and the guys wanted to show this one more time," ORT correspondent Viktor Dyatlikovich said.

Lukashenko was also clearly annoyed with Moscow for stepping up checks on the Belarussian border despite a customs union deal between the two countries. Russia fears that contraband is crossing into Russia through Belarus from Ukraine, Baltic states and further afield.
"We agreed customs between Belarus and Russia have been removed, but no, some further control is required from a state, with which we are in a single union in fact," he said.
"We will control all our border territory, including with Russia, as she (Russia) controls it now, though this already looks dishonourable," he said.

Interfax said Lukashenko had ordered extra guards to the borders weeks ago and quoted him saying: "I think we will instal order with the arrival of new border forces chief General Alexander Pavlovsky. We will back and help the border guards."

Harsh words had already been exchanged by Lukashenko and Russian President Boris Yeltsin over the arrest of the first ORT crew, with Yeltsin saying he might review a union treaty signed this year on integration between the two countries.

Belarus has never enjoyed a prolonged period of independence and the language of choice is Russian. Lukashenko's policy of forming a union with Russia has brought him popularity, but relations with Moscow have not always been smooth and Russian media often criticise him.
Lukashenko has often accused Russian media of portraying his leadership in an unfairly negative light.
He accused the ORT journalists of being in the pay of unnamed foreign powers and said he had no right to free them.
A European Union official in Minsk to mediate talks with the opposition said he had asked the president to free the crew but Lukashenko responded that it was a matter for the courts.

Russian television crews have been denied access to feed pictures to Moscow and Western officials and institutions have accused Minsk of placing stringent curbs on the media and violating other human rights.
